title: Notes Java Uses Of Super Final Keyword

runs.text: 1. What is the final keyword in Java, and where can it be applied?
The final keyword is used to restrict modification in Java. It can be applied to three things:
Class
Method
Variable
When applied to a class, it prevents inheritance. When applied to a method, it prevents overriding. When applied to a variable, its value cannot be reassigned after initialization.
Therefore, final is mainly associated with restricting
a value
or
an implementation
2. What happens when the final keyword is applied to a class, method, and variable?
When a class is declared as final, no other class can inherit from it.
When a method is declared as final, a child class cannot override that method.
When a variable is declared as final, its value cannot be reassigned after it has been initialized.
A class is normally made final when it should not have any subclasses. In an inheritance hierarchy, leaf classes can be declared as final.
For example:

blocks.text:
final class HomeSparrow extends Sparrow {
}

runs.text: Another class cannot extend
HomeSparrow

A final method can still be overloaded. Method overloading means defining multiple methods with the same name but different signatures.

4. What happens when a variable is declared as final, and how do final local and instance variables differ in initialization?
A final variable cannot be assigned a new value after it has been initialized.
For example:
The statement
a = 20; causes a compilation error because a has already been initialized.
A final local variable can be declared first and initialized later:

blocks.text:
final int a;
a = 20;

runs.text: This is valid because the variable is initialized only once.

A final instance variable cannot be left uninitialized in its declaration and assigned arbitrarily later through a method. It must be properly initialized as part of instance initialization, such as through its declaration or constructor.
For example:
After initialization, a cannot be reassigned.
5. Which combinations involving final were examined, and what are their valid uses?
A static method can be declared as final.
A static variable can be declared as final.
A method parameter can be declared as final.
A setter or getter can be declared as final because they are methods.
A constructor cannot be declared as final.
An instance block cannot be declared as final.
A local variable cannot be declared as static, even when it is declared inside a static method. Any variable declared inside a method is a local variable, and local variables cannot be static.
The final keyword applies to values or implementations; it is not applied to method names, keywords, brackets, or symbols.
6. What is the difference between local, instance, and static variables in Java?
A local variable is declared inside a method.
An instance variable is declared inside a class but outside a method without using static.
A static variable is declared inside a class but outside a method using the static keyword.

rows: Inside a class, outside a method
Inside a class, outside a method using static

runs.text: A local variable is associated with the method's stack frame. An instance variable is associated with the object in heap memory. A static variable is associated with the static area.

A local variable belongs to a method and is created when the method is called.
A static variable belongs to the class and is created when the class is loaded.
Since a variable declared inside a method is always a local variable, it cannot be declared as static.
This rule is the same whether the method itself is static or
instance-based

A variable should be static when its value is common to all objects of the class.
A variable should be instance-based when its value is specific to an individual object.

17. What are instance blocks and constructors used for, and how do they differ?
An instance block is used for instance-level initialization, particularly when common initialization logic needs to be executed for objects.
A constructor is also used to initialize an object and is specifically associated with object construction.
A constructor can accept parameters and can be overloaded, whereas an instance block does not have constructor-style parameterization or overloading.

Constructor overloading means defining multiple constructors in the same class with the same name but different signatures.
The signature can differ in:
Number of parameters

If no constructor is explicitly defined in a class, the compiler provides a zero-parameter constructor called the default constructor.
The default constructor contains a call to the parent class constructor.

21. What is encapsulation in Java, and how is it achieved?
Encapsulation is the binding of data members and methods into a single unit while providing controlled access to the data.
Encapsulation is achieved using both:
Private data members
Getter and setter methods
For example:
The private keyword restricts direct access to the variable, while getter and setter methods provide controlled access.
The main advantage of encapsulation is data security.

24. What are the types of inheritance, and which types are supported through Java classes?
The commonly identified types of inheritance are:
Single inheritance
Multilevel inheritance
Hierarchical inheritance
Multiple inheritance
Hybrid inheritance
Cyclic inheritance
Multiple inheritance is not supported through Java classes because it can lead to ambiguity when multiple parent classes provide the same behavior.
Cyclic inheritance is also not permitted because it would create an infinite inheritance and constructor chain.
25. What is the role of the Object class in Java inheritance?
Object is the default root class of the Java class hierarchy.
If a class does not explicitly extend another class, it ultimately inherits from Object.
Therefore, the inheritance hierarchy of Java classes ultimately leads to the Object class.
26. Why is cyclic inheritance not permitted in Java?
Cyclic inheritance occurs when classes form a circular inheritance relationship.
For example:
A extends B
B extends A
Such a structure would result in an infinite inheritance and constructor chain.
Therefore, cyclic inheritance is not permitted.

28. Why is constructor chaining important in inheritance?
Constructor chaining ensures that the initialization performed by parent classes is completed before the child class is initialized.
For example, if a parent class initializes properties such as A and B, the child class can acquire those initialized properties through inheritance instead of initializing them again.
This supports code reusability, which is an important purpose of inheritance.
